messages.name: lookup_refund_policy
messages.content: {"ok": true, "sections": [{"citation": "refund-policy/v2/window", "title": "Time limit", "text": "A refund must be requested no later than 30 days after the delivery time recorded on the order. Days are exact periods of twenty-four hours, and a request at exactly the deadline is on time. The request time is the moment the shop creates the refund proposal. If an earlier proposal for the same units was created in time and then expired, or stopped being valid because the order or this policy changed, before it was paid, a later request for those units is not refused for being late: a staff member takes the case. A proposal that the customer replaced or cancelled, that a staff member rejected, or that a handoff closed does not count. A request for an exception to the time limit is refused with this reason."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/eligible-orders", "title": "Which orders qualify", "text": "Only orders with the status \"delivered\" can receive a refund. An order that has not been delivered is not refunded through this process: the assistant tells the customer the order's status, and cancelling the order or changing its delivery is outside this process, so the assistant offers a staff member for that. If an order is recorded as delivered but the customer says it never arrived, a staff member takes the case. If a delivered order has no delivery time, or one that cannot be right (before the purchase or in the future), a staff member takes the case."}, {"citation": "refund-policy/v2/exceptions", "title": "Exceptions and talking to a person", "text": "A person takes over the conversation when the customer asks for one, at any time; when the shop's decision on a request is that a staff member takes the case; or in a case this policy names: units the customer says were sent but have not arrived, a delivered order the customer says never arrived, and a request to refund shipping. A request for an exception to a rule of this policy is refused with that rule's reason, because a staff member cannot approve a refund this policy does not allow. A request one rule refuses does not become a staff case because of another rule: only the customer's request for a person, or a case named above, makes it one. After a refusal the assistant gives the reason, and the customer can still ask for a person. A question this policy does not answer, such as cancelling an order on its way, is answered as far as the policy goes, and a person is offered, not imposed. When a person takes over, every proposal of the conversation that is not paid is closed, and the person continues from there; a refund already paid stays paid."}], "note": "Cite a section by its citation ID, exactly as given."}
